verdict.headline: AI earnings trifecta — Nvidia, Salesforce, CrowdStrike all beat; only tech advances
verdict.label: Three AI beat-and-raises in one session; ten S&P sectors negative; Warsh keynote Friday resets the rate path
verdict.rationale_short: NVDA, Salesforce, and CrowdStrike confirmed AI revenue actualization across hardware, software, and security in a single session, with the Nasdaq +1.57% while all other S&P 500 sectors closed negative. AMD held below $484 for the fifteenth consecutive session despite the strongest possible AI backdrop — distribution, not accumulation. The read holds if the 30Y stays below 5.25% through Warsh's Friday keynote; a hawkish framing would stress-test narrowing tech leadership at expanded multiples.

trade_setups.thesis: Fifteen consecutive sessions below $484, including Thursday's three-AI-beat backdrop. The market is not treating the AI cycle as AMD-inclusive even when NVDA, CRM, and CRWD deliver simultaneously.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive regular-session closes above $484 with above-average volume confirm the break. Fade below $460 on volume — particularly alongside a hawkish Warsh — would be a qualitatively different signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: Two consecutive closes above $484 on volume above 30-day average.

trade_setups.thesis: Double beat with raised guidance sold off AH on margin concerns — consistent with the CSCO and AMAT altitude templates from August 12-13. Google custom-silicon deal confirmed; this is not a fundamental miss.
trade_setups.entry: Friday regular-session close is the defining tell. Below $230 confirms distribution at altitude; recovery above $245 absorbs the AH move as position-unwinding on a 187% YTD run.
trade_setups.invalidation: Regular-session close above $245 on Friday with volume.

trade_setups.asset: SPX breadth divergence vs. Warsh rate risk
trade_setups.thesis: All ten non-tech S&P sectors closed negative on the strongest single-session AI earnings day in over a year. A hawkish Warsh would stress-test this configuration simultaneously from the rate side.
trade_setups.entry: SPX 7,726 is the reference close. Below 7,650 post-Warsh would confirm breadth deterioration is spreading. Above 7,800 with non-tech sectors recovering would confirm the divergence has resolved.
trade_setups.invalidation: Six or more S&P 500 sectors closing positive simultaneously.

bear_case: Thursday's breadth tells a different story than its headline. All ten non-tech sectors closed negative on the strongest AI earnings day in over a year — the same narrowing leadership pattern that preceded the August 24 selloff. AMD closing below $484 for the fifteenth consecutive session despite the most favorable backdrop of the cycle signals institutional money does not view the AI earnings surge as sector-wide. If Warsh frames Canada tariff cost-push (September 8 effective) plus 3.7% headline PCE as non-transitory inflation — pushing the 30Y above 5.25% — rate pressure lands on a market with stretched tech multiples and deteriorating breadth simultaneously. If SPX closes below 7,600 post-Warsh, this read no longer holds.
